cells.tense: You're holding the structure and it's holding everything else, steady in your hands right now.
cells.ask: offer the next thing you've been keeping in the back of your mind — the one that comes before you're sure why, and let it land without checking it
cells.core:
You give things a shape that actually fits them. People walk into what you've organized and the mess gets smaller — not because you forced it, but because you saw where each piece belonged and set it there. That's not control. Control leaves no room for anything it didn't plan for. What you build leaves room, which is why it holds.

There's something you already know about what comes next here — nothing argued for it, it just arrived — and you haven't acted on it. Handing that over costs nothing and it's the next thing this steadiness is free to feed.
cells.sheetLine: You're giving what's tangled a shape that fits, and it's working.
cells.verb: building the frame that lets what's tangled get navigated
cells.place: in the part of a life where what's finished has to end for what's next to begin

cells.tense: You're bracing against something ahead that hasn't happened, holding a shape you're already sure you'll need.
cells.ask: look at one ending you're managing and ask what it actually is underneath the shape you've given it, then let that answer matter more than the plan
cells.core:
When this is working, you make the ending navigable. You give the thing that's finishing a shape people can move through — where the pieces go, what comes after, who does what. The mess gets smaller because you saw where each part belonged. That's the gift of this seat, and it's a real one.

But somewhere in there the structure stopped serving what it holds and started replacing it. What's ending is being organized instead of allowed to end. The frame is getting all your attention and the thing inside it is getting none. Stand back from the arrangement and see the shape of what's going on, not the version you built to handle it. Whatever you notice from there is truer than the plan.
cells.sheetLine: You've built a structure around an ending, and the structure has become the thing.
cells.verb: building the frame that lets what's tangled get navigated

cells.tense: You stopped building the structure and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: name the one false shape you've been carrying — the rule or setup that was never real — and let that one fall; the rest can wait
cells.core:
When this is working, you decide what goes and what stays, and then it's done. You look at what's ending and give it a shape — this piece stays, this piece goes, here's what comes after — and people can move through the ending because you made it navigable. That's what this seat does when it's alive.

Right now nothing sorts. Everything is as important as everything else, and the pieces don't assemble into anything you'd call a shape. You're not disorganized by nature. Something got cleared and you stopped setting anything in its place. One structure you're still holding didn't earn its place. Say it out loud as the false thing it is and drop it. That alone rebuilds more than any plan you could make.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped clearing and nothing has assembled since.

cells.tense: You're already arranging things for the people around you, and you'd say you don't have it together at all.
cells.ask: name one ending you already know is coming for someone near you, and say out loud to yourself that you saw it — claim the seeing as yours
cells.core:
When this is working, things make sense in your presence. People bring you what's tangled and walk away with it sorted — not because you told them what to do, but because the shape you gave it was true. You do this with endings too. You see what's finishing before anyone says so, and you quietly arrange for it.

That's happening right now. People come to you and things make sense, and it happens without you noticing you're doing it. When you look at your own life, though, it reads like a mess you haven't gotten around to — that's the gap between what your hands are doing and what you'd put your name on. There's an ending you already see clearly for someone close to you. You've seen it and been calling it nothing. It's not nothing. It's yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're already giving things a shape. You just don't count it as yours.
